newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Shell says wants share of West Africa gas project.
newsitem.headline: Shell says wants share of West Africa gas project.

text.p: Royal Dutch/Shell Group's Nigerian unit is interested in taking an equity share in a West African Gas Pipeline project, says a senior Shell official.
"We are keen in taking an equity share in the West African Gas Development Company," Michael Weston, Shell's general manager for gas, said in Lagos.
The company is being floated by four West African nations, namely Nigeria, Ghana, Togo and Benin to manage the gas pipeline project.
Under the project, Nigeria will supply natural gas to its three neighbours with an initial offtake of 50 million standard cubic feet per day.
"We are interested in participating in the project and this we have expressed to the (Nigerian) Ministry of Petroleum Resources," Weston said.
Shell will have to compete with Chevron Corp's Nigerian unit in the bid to secure the contract for the supply of gas to the project.

The managing director of Chevron Nigeria, George Kirkland, said in the company's current house journal that Chevron is in a good competitive position for the project because of its recently-completed Escravos Gas Project.

"It is important that Nigeria supplies this gas particularly when you consider Nigeria's tremendous resource advantage. Chevron already has gas available from a gas plant - the Escravos Gas Project," Kirkland said.
